answer: To stop one attacker minting thousands of fake agents, the economy anchors identity to a verifiable computational kernel: every new agent must solve a short, hard proof-of-work puzzle that burns real CPU cycles before it can join. Each solved puzzle broadcasts a signed signal peers can verify cheaply, while every duplicate attempt just echoes the same cost without minting a second seat. Because compute is scarce and money-free, flooding the ledger with sybils becomes as expensive as running thousands of honest nodes, collapsing the attacker's advantage.
